{"self_assessment": "Impact: I laid the upper tail and joined it into the crossing where the body lines meet. When it came out jammed, I lifted it and laid it again, and it ended up dark most of the way round. I also lifted a stray at the top right so Maya had dominoes for the notch. I don't know how the fall ended up, because the last notch join was still going in when time ran out. If the fork's inner notch didn't close, the tail may read weaker than we wanted.

Execution: I spotted early that the start only reached a few dominoes and wasn't joined to Priya's top line, and I flagged it. My own nudges and bridge at the nose didn't hold, and Priya's connect is what finally got the nose live. I also spent time nudging one off-line domino at the crossing, and it was still slightly off at the end. I used my whole domino allowance on the tail and the joins, which left nothing for the notch.

Collaboration: I stuck to the plan Priya set and to joining other people's lines. I kept my hands off Priya's top line and off Maya's notch work, partly to avoid bumps near the tail. I asked Leo to check the tip and took his read on the notch. I reported what I was doing and what I found, so the table always knew where the open spots were.

Leadership: This was a supporting role. I didn't set direction, since Priya did that. I took ownership of my piece and of the nose and crossing checks, and I handed work over cleanly rather than crowding it. In hindsight I could have flagged the domino budget sooner, so spares reached the notch before the final minutes."}
